payload.text:
Prove this Lean 4 theorem (source: FATE-M, difficulty: easy).

Informal statement:
Let g be the pair consisting of a in G and b in H. If a has order m and b has order n, then g has order equal to the least common multiple of m and n.

Formal statement to prove:
theorem fatem_041_orderOf_prod {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] {a : G} {b : H} :
    orderOf (a, b) = Nat.lcm (orderOf a) (orderOf b)

The reasoner should give a strategy (use search_lemmas to find relevant Mathlib results), the engineer should formalise and verify with check_lean, and the critic should review faithfulness.

IsOfFinOrder.prod_mk : IsOfFinOrder a → IsOfFinOrder b → IsOfFinOrder (a, b)  -- Product of Finite Order Elements Has Finite Order
Pi.orderOf  [Fintype ι] (x : ∀ i, α i) : orderOf x = Finset.univ.lcm (fun i => orderOf (x i))  -- Order of Product Element Equals LCM of Component Orders
IsOfFinOrder.mul  (hx : IsOfFinOrder x) (hy : IsOfFinOrder y) : IsOfFinOrder (x * y)  -- Product of Elements of Finite Order in a Commutative Monoid is of Finite Order
Prod.orderOf  (x : α × β) : orderOf x = (orderOf x.1).lcm (orderOf x.2)  -- Order of Element in Product Monoid is LCM of Component Orders
